documents.title: Annual Physical Exam
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
55 y/o M for annual exam. Brought a list of diet questions.

Main question: over the summer he read several pieces saying a glass of wine a day is good for the heart, so he began having one 5 oz glass of red with dinner every night. Wants to know if he should keep it up, given his dad's MI.

Otherwise well. No chest pain or SOB. No abdominal pain, diverticulitis quiet since 2017. Saw optometry in June, no retinopathy.

Meds: lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, metformin 1000 mg BID. Taking them all.
Allergies: NKDA.
FHx: father MI age 58, mother T2DM, brother HTN.
Social: quit cigarettes 2016. Wine as above, no other alcohol.

Exam: BP 135/85. Well appearing. HEENT, neck normal. Heart regular, no murmurs. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. No edema. Foot exam: sensation and pulses intact, no skin breakdown. Exam otherwise unremarkable.

Labs 10/8: TC 195, HDL 40, LDL 120, TG 175. Fasting glucose 98. CMP and CBC unremarkable, A1c in range.

Assessment/plan:
1. Alcohol and heart health: talked through what those studies actually show. They compare people who happen to drink a little with people who don't, and the non-drinkers include people who quit for health reasons; moderate drinkers also tend to differ in income, diet and exercise. That makes the apparent benefit hard to trust. I would not start or keep drinking for heart protection. One glass with dinner is within low-risk limits and his call; didn't want him to go above that. Better payoff from diet, walking and his statin.
2. HTN: BP a little above my goal for a diabetic. Continue lisinopril 20, recheck at next visit.
3. Mixed hyperlipidemia: LDL 120 on atorvastatin 40, HDL 40. Diet review, less refined carbs, more fiber. Continue statin. Recheck lipids in spring.
4. T2DM: stable, continue metformin.
5. HM: flu vaccine today. COVID series done in spring. PSA due next year.
Follow up 6 months with fasting labs before.

documents.title: Follow-up: cholesterol, diabetes
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Subjective: Back for the 6 month check on lipids and sugar after his October physical. No complaints. Has been doing a lot of reading online about statins and now has two worries: that atorvastatin will damage his liver, and that statins cause diabetes. Says he's half decided to quit it. No muscle aches. Still on lisinopril 20 and metformin 1000 BID. Still 1 glass of wine with dinner.

Objective: BP 132/84. Exam unremarkable: heart RRR, lungs clear, abdomen soft and nontender, no edema.
Labs 4/19: TC 190, LDL 100, HDL 45, TG 150. Fasting glucose 98. Liver panel normal.

Assessment and plan:
Mixed hyperlipidemia with diabetes, HTN and a father with an MI at 58: he is exactly the person a statin helps.
- Liver: serious liver injury from statins is rare; his liver tests are normal after years on it. We'd keep checking.
- Diabetes: statins can nudge glucose up slightly, and he already has diabetes; the heart attack and stroke reduction far outweighs that, and his sugars are well controlled.
- LDL improved to 100 from 120 since fall with his diet changes, which is real progress.
He agrees to stay on atorvastatin 40 for now. Gave him a printed summary to read.
HTN: better today, continue lisinopril.
T2DM: continue metformin.
RTC for physical in the fall.

Doing fine. Stayed on the atorvastatin after our talk in April. Still one glass of wine at dinner. Did not get to the eye doctor this year, says he will.
Meds: lisinopril 20 qd, atorvastatin 40 qd, metformin 1000 bid. NKDA.
ROS: negative.
Exam: Vitals reviewed. General well. Fundi not examined. Neck without bruit. Heart S1 S2 normal, regular. Lungs clear. Abd soft, nontender, no hernia. Ext no edema. Feet: no lesions, protective sensation intact, DP and PT pulses palpable.
PHQ-2: 0.
A/P
# HTN: controlled. Continue.
# T2DM: labs today. Needs eye exam.
# Mixed HLD: lipids today, continue statin.
# HM: flu, PCV20 (diabetes indication), and bivalent COVID booster today, pt agreeable to all three. PSA today after discussing pros and cons. Colonoscopy due 2027.
RTC 4 months.
